narrative:
On August 5, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 38.4%, with 1,095 out of 2,849 scheduled cases heard across 46 judges. This reflects a slight decrease in conversion efficiency compared to August 4 (39.8%, 1,013 of 2,546 heard) and August 3 (44.5%, 1,103 of 2,478 heard), even as the total court docket grew by over 300 scheduled cases day-over-day.

Judicial output varied across court halls. The bench of D. K. Singh & T. M. Nadaf (Hall 4) achieved a high conversion rate of 81.4% (35 of 43 scheduled cases heard), while single benches led by Vijaykumar A. Patil (Hall 32) and V. Srishananda (Hall 21) converted 80.8% (42 of 52) and 74.8% (86 of 115) of their respective lists. Justice M. Nagaprasanna managed the highest absolute workload, taking up 140 matters across multiple list splits. Conversely, Hall 6 under B. M. Shyam Prasad recorded minimal progress, hearing 1 of 298 scheduled cases.

Stage-wise performance showed that procedural matters in the Orders stage comprised the largest portion of the docket (1,093 scheduled, 386 heard; 35.3%), whereas Final Hearing matters exhibited a lower conversion rate of 16.1% (73 of 454 heard). Preliminary Hearings maintained higher efficiency at 47.3% (173 of 366 heard). By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) represented the heaviest workload at 1,326 scheduled and 461 heard (34.8%), expanding from 1,188 scheduled on August 4. Regular Second Appeals (RSA) saw high clearance efficiency at 71.9% (97 of 135 heard), whereas Civil Revision Petitions (CRP) had the lowest clearance rate at 8.9% (4 of 45 heard).
